title: How big is the US market for dog food each year? A worked market sizing answer
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How big is the US market for dog food each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Here is a step up to practise on. Read the question, pause, and have a go at your own estimate first, even a rough one. Then walk through the answer below and compare. Your number does not need to match; your logic is what counts.
body:
The question

How big is the US market for dog food each year?

The approach

Households × share with dogs × dogs per household × spend per dog.

Say this out loud before you touch any numbers. It lets the interviewer agree with your plan, or nudge you, before you have done any work.

Step by step

  1. US households: 130M
  2. × 38% own a dog
  3. × 1.5 dogs per dog-owning household
  4. × $500 food spend per dog per year

That gives about $37.1B a year.

Does it make sense?

About $40 a month per dog, which is in line with a mid-priced bag of dry food.

This sanity check is the step most people skip, and one of the easiest ways to impress. It shows you care whether the number is right, not just whether the sum works.

Your turn

outro: If your estimate was far off, look for which step made the difference. That is where the learning is, and it is exactly what an interviewer would ask about.
